# 4 Maccabees Chapter 18 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** Conclusion: Epilogue of Praise

---

**18:1** O Israelite children, descendants of the seed of Abraham, obey this law and exercise piety in every way,

**18:2** knowing that devout reason is master of all passions, not only of pains from within but of those from without as well.

**18:3** For this reason those men gave up their bodies to the pain of torments for the sake of God.

**18:4** And it was through the blood of those devout ones and their death as an atoning sacrifice that divine providence preserved Israel that had previously been afflicted.

**18:5** For the tyrant Antiochus, when he saw the courage of their virtue and their endurance under the tortures, proclaimed them to his soldiers as an example of endurance.

**18:6** And this made them ashamed and courageous for the battle and for patient endurance, so that the enemy could not subdue the nation even by great force and so gave up the attempt.

**18:7** Thus through the nobility of those who died for God, reason is proved sovereign over the passions.

**18:8** But it would be wrong for me not to mention also the courage of the mother as worthy of more than praise.

**18:9** For though she saw seven sons die in the space of a single day, because of the hope she had in God she endured this heroically.

**18:10** She exhorted each one of them in the language of their fathers, being filled with a noble spirit.

**18:11** She said to them: My sons, I brought you forth from the womb; I nursed you for three years; I reared you and took you to this point of life.

**18:12** I urge you, my children, to look at the heaven and earth and to see all that is in them, and thus to know that it was not out of existing things that God made them, nor did the human race come into being from existing things.

**18:13** Do not be afraid of this tormentor, but be worthy of your brothers.

**18:14** Accept death, so that in God's mercy I may receive you again with your brothers.

**18:15** While she was yet speaking these words, the youngest son spoke up and said: O guardians of the law, O friends of virtue, death is not a terror to those who live virtuously.

**18:16** This most holy and pious mother, filled with joy at the noble deaths of her sons and not grieved at their deaths, urged them on to die for the sake of God, saying to each:

**18:17** Be courageous, my children! Do not be afraid of death! For if you are faithful to the law, God will grant you a glorious resurrection.

**18:18** She herself then put the crown on her own faithfulness by following her sons in death.

**18:19** And I call blessed and holy those who died in this way for the sake of God.

**18:20** For they overcame the tyrant by their endurance, and through them their nation was purified.

**18:21** Let us therefore end our discourse with this conclusion: devout reason is the sovereign master of the passions, as the examples of Eleazar, the seven brothers, and the mother have proved.

**18:22** They overcame the passions; they conquered the tyrant; they won the prizes of immortality.

**18:23** They were righteous, and they kept faith with God in life and in death.

**18:24** Blessed indeed and most holy are the memories of Eleazar, the seven brothers, and the mother, for they fought for the honor of God.

**18:25** And their souls are now with God, and God himself will honor them forever.
